data.narrative:
Core Automation is a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, currently targeting a Series funding round of $500M–$1B at a $4–5B+ valuation. The broader AI & Software sector comprises 16 peer companies; however, the comp universe for direct valuation work is constrained, with 1 public comparable (Palantir, PLTR) and 8 private peers including Palantir, Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, and Reflection AI.

Peer-median analysis is not applicable to this valuation. The dataset identified zero same-stage comparables, zero adjacent-stage comparables, and zero similar-valuation-tier peers meeting narrow filter criteria. The 16 same-sector companies in the dataset do not yield the three minimum datapoints needed to anchor a robust median multiple. A fallback to all-sector median multiples would introduce excessive noise and misrepresentation given Core Automation's specific frontier-tech positioning.

Given the inapplicability of quantitative triangulation methods, this valuation lacks sufficient granular peer data to derive a defensible range through comparable-company analysis. The stated target of $4–5B+ remains the primary reference point, though it reflects the company's capital-raising objective rather than independent analytical support. Key uncertainties include the absence of financial metrics (revenue, burn, path to profitability) and the nascent, differentiated nature of the opportunity, which limits reliance on traditional sector multiples. Further diligence on unit economics and market sizing would be necessary to validate valuation assumptions.
